extracted.intended_audience: patent classifiers, patent examiners, and patent office patent-information specialists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assigning International Patent Classification (IPC) places, indexing codes, and multiple classifications to patent documents and their constituent inventive subjects, including special rules for chemical matter, combinations, libraries, indexing schemes, and classification at different publication levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function-oriented and application-oriented places
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish places that classify a 'thing in general' by its intrinsic nature or function (function-oriented places) from places for a thing 'specially adapted for' a particular use, its particular use, or its incorporation into a larger system (application-oriented places).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function-oriented places cover technical subjects independent of field of use (examples: valves characterised by construction not depending on fluid type; compounds characterised by chemical structure). Application-oriented places cover matter specially adapted for a given purpose or incorporated into systems (examples: heart valve insertion, filters adapted for particular purposes, leaf spring in vehicle suspension). A given place may be partially function- and partially application-oriented; relative degree is not absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to classify in function-oriented vs application-oriented places
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is unclear whether to classify in a function-oriented or application-oriented place, apply the rules in paragraph 90.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) If a particular application is mentioned but not specifically disclosed or fully identified, classify in the function-oriented place if available. (b) If essential technical characteristics relate both to intrinsic nature and to particular use/incorporation, classify in both function- and application-oriented places if available. (c) If (a) and (b) cannot be used, classify in both the function-oriented place and relevant application-oriented places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of larger systems and their parts
rubrics_metrics.description: When classifying a larger system (combination) as a whole, identify and separately classify parts or details that are novel and unobvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the document in the place for the larger system and also classify the thing itself if the thing (part) is novel and unobvious. Example: classify both vehicle-wheel suspension (B60G) and a novel leaf spring itself (F16F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing places when category not in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: If a category of subject matter (one way of expressing the technical subject) has no distinct place in titles, use the most appropriate existing place for other categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if titles do not indicate suitability, use references, notes, definitions, or provisions for similar subject matter in related groups to identify appropriate places. Consult definitions where present for guidance on related categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of chemical compounds (per se)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical compounds per se are classified in section C according to chemical structure; if a specific field of use is an essential technical characteristic, also classify in the place for that field of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the compound is known and only its application is new, classify only in the place covering the field of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of chemical mixtures or compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify mixtures/compositions per se according to chemical composition place if such a place exists; otherwise classify by use or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both composition and use constitute essential technical characteristics, classify according to both. If the mixture is known and only its use is new, classify only in the place for the field of use. Examples: C03C (glass), C08L (organic macromolecular compositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of preparation or treatment of compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes for preparation or treatment of a chemical compound are classified in the place for that process; if no such place exists, classify in the place of the compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the resulting compound is novel, also classify the compound according to chemical structure. General processes for classes of compounds are classified in groups for the processes employed, when such groups exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of apparatus or processes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subject concerns an apparatus, classify in the place for the apparatus; if no apparatus place exists, classify in the place for the process performed by that apparatus. Conversely, processes are classified in the place for the process, or in the apparatus place if the process place does not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no place exists for the manufacture of a product, classify the manufacturing apparatus or process in the place covering the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of articles of manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify an article in the place for the article; if no such place exists, classify in the appropriate function-oriented place or, if not possible, by field of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a glue-dispenser for bookbinding is classified in B42C 9/00 (applying glue peculiar to bookbinding) because no specific place exists for glue-dispensers for bookbinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of multistep processes and industrial plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Multistep processes or industrial plants that are combinations of steps or apparatus are classified as a whole in places provided for such combinations; if none exist, classify in the place for the product obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an element of the combination (e.g., a process step or machine) is also inventive, classify that element separately as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of details and constructional parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for classifying constructional or functional details or parts of subject matter, including applicability across kinds of subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Details only applicable to one kind are classified in details places of that kind if they exist. (b) If such places do not exist, classify details in the place for the subject matter. (c) Details applicable to more than one kind are classified in more general details places if they exist. (d) If general places do not exist, classify according to all kinds to which they explicitly apply. Example: umbrella details in A45B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of general chemical formulae (Markush-type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for classifying general chemical formulae that cover large sets of related compounds and may map to many classification places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Classify all 'fully identified' compounds that are novel and unobvious if they are (i) specifically claimed as such or in a composition, (ii) products of a claimed process, or (iii) derivatives. A 'fully identified' compound has exact structure by name/formula or deducible from preparation with not more than one alternative and is characterised by a physical property or worked example. Step 2: If no fully identified compounds are disclosed, classify the general formula in the most specific group(s) that cover most potential embodiments, limited to a single or very small number of groups. Step 3: Optional (non-obligatory) classification of other compounds within scope may be made. If classifying all fully identified compounds would lead to many symbols (e.g., >20) and many subgroups under one higher group, the classifier may reduce symbols by classifying at the higher group only; otherwise classify in all more specific subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of combinatorial libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: For libraries composed of many compounds or entities, classify only individually 'fully identified' members obligatorily; classify the library as a whole in an appropriate library group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fully identified members are classified into the groups that most specifically provide for them (e.g., section C). The library as a whole is classified in an appropriate group such as subclass C40B. Non-obligatory classifications may be added when other members are of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple classification and its purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple classification is needed when different categories of subject matter (processes, products, apparatus, materials) or multiple aspects of a subject are invention information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple classification (and indexing) facilitates search; it is recommended but not always obligatory. Identify all aspects where non-trivial inventive information exists and classify each as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-aspect classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply multi-aspect classification to subject matter characterised by several aspects (e.g., intrinsic structure and particular use) so that classification is not restricted to a single aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places where multi-aspect classification is especially desirable are indicated by notes. Such notes may prescribe obligatory supplementary classification for indicated aspects or recommend multi-aspect classification to increase search efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schemes for secondary classification
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain technical subjects, obligatory supplementary classification schemes are provided to classify a different aspect of subject matter already obligatorily classified elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include subclass A01P (biocidal/pest activity) and subclass A61P (therapeutic activity) used as secondary classification schemes when therapeutic/functional activities are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid systems and indexing schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid systems couple a classification scheme with a complementary indexing scheme to specify additional aspects not covered by classification place titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying in a hybrid system, first assign all appropriate classification symbols, then add any indexing codes that identify additional elements useful for search. Indexing codes usually start at 101/00 and have numbering distinct from classification symbols; some subclasses are used only for indexing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of indexing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing codes may be applied to identify elements of information about an already-classified technical subject useful for search purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hierarchically lowest indexing group that provides for the element. Use the higher group only residually to record features not covered in subdivisions. When indexing two or more elements, apply the lowest appropriate indexing groups for each. Avoid indexing very general main groups that give no useful search information (example: do not apply an overly general indexing code such as B23K 101/00 when more specific codes exist like 101/26 for rails and 101/28 for beams). Indexing codes can only be applied in association with classification symbols and are indicated by notes where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligatory classification (invention information must be classified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent authorities must indicate the complete classification symbols of the Classification applied to the invention information in a patent document (Article 4(3) of the Strasbourg Agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification symbols representing invention information are obligatory and must be allotted by the competent authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-obligatory classification and indexing (additional information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional (non-invention) information may be classified or indexed but such classification/indexing is discretionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is desirable to classify or index additional information since it may be useful for future search and patenting, but recommendations in places are advisory and do not make such classification obligatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification procedure for patents granted after search and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: For granted patents that have been searched and examined, classify all subject matter covered by the claims that is novel and unobvious and any novel/unobvious constituents or subcombinations; also classify unclaimed disclosure that is novel and unobvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification should be based on each claim as a whole and each inventive embodiment within a claim. It is desirable to classify/index additional useful information complementing invention information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of searched but unexamined patent documents (published applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify all claimed subject matter that appears to be novel and unobvious in view of the search results, plus any unclaimed disclosure that appears novel and unobvious in view of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable to classify/index additional information complementing invention information if useful for search purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of unsearched patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For unsearched publications, classify all claimed subject matter that is potentially novel and unobvious according to the opinion of a classifier expert; also classify potentially novel/unobvious unclaimed disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the classifier is not an expert in the art, use all claims to determine subject matter to be classified. As with other levels, it's desirable to classify/index additional information useful for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: General observations on number and review of classification symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent documents should not be classified as a single unit; identify and separately classify all different inventive things. There are rules about unclaimed subject matter, minimum symbols, and review to avoid unnecessary symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different inventive things include different claims, alternative variants, or different categories of subject matter (e.g., product and method). Unclaimed invention information need not be classified if fully identified in a related published application from the same office. If no invention information is present, at least one classification symbol must still be assigned based on the portion most useful for search. Review earlier-stage classifications at later stages (grant/search/abandonment) to minimize unnecessary symbols, noting some offices do not re-classify published applications when patents are granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a subclass (hierarchical procedure and alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine invention and additional information, then select the most appropriate subclass using the hierarchical IPC structure or alternative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hierarchy approach: identify section, subsection, class, then subclass; remember titles give broad indication only. Alternatives: use the alphabetical Catchword Index, text searching in the IPC or catchword index, and review classification symbols of related patent documents (statistical/text-search analysis). Verify any selected place by checking scope, references and notes of the subclass and its superior places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a group — general rules and the common rule
rubrics_metrics.description: After subclass selection, determine main group/subgroup applying the general classification rule used in that subclass (common rule, first place priority, last place priority) and any special rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common rule (default): assumes places are mutually exclusive; where several groups might apply, apply priority principles to limit unnecessary multiple classification: (a) groups for more complex matter take priority over less complex (combinations over subcombinations; whole things over details); (b) more specialised groups take priority over less specialised. Use the standardised sequence of main groups as guidance, but in common rule areas classification should be made in all appropriate places rather than applying priority between similar groups. Procedure: (a) check if only one group provides for the subject; if so proceed to step (c). (b) If multiple groups apply, use priority principles to select group(s); if priority exists select that group (others may also be selected if useful). If no priority can be determined, apply step (c) separately for each group. (c) Repeat at each hierarchical level until no further subgroups provide for the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no specific place for a combination exists
rubrics_metrics.description: When a combination has no specific place in an area where the common rule applies, classify according to its subcombinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the priority principles for selecting among subcombinations; subcombinations not selected for obligatory classification should be considered for classification as additional information.
